1.why: verify-token compares the SHA-256 hash of the submitted code against the recovery bound to the caller's session (currentRecovery enforces recovery.sessionId === session.id), so a code is only accepted for its owning session.

2.why: False: currentRecovery returns undefined for any session that does not own the recovery, so the same reset code cannot be used by another user/session.

3.why: There are no account login sessions that could persist, and after completion the recovery cannot be reused (endpoints return 403), though the recovery session cookie itself is not explicitly invalidated on completion.

4.why: Bun.serve is TLS-only with an HSTS header and non-https request URLs are rejected, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest version in the configuration.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests and passwords as Argon2id hashes with plaintext never stored, though these are hashing rather than encryption algorithms.

6.why: No email message exists; delivery is simulated in-browser with the token returned only to the owning HTTPS session, so email-specific data guarding is not applicable.

7.why: All user inputs are validated against strict allowlists (contact regex, 64-char hex token, 6-digit MFA code), JSON bodies are type- and size-checked, and rendering uses textContent only.

8.why: There are no outbound redirects at all; navigation is same-page hash routing and CSP restricts form-action and connect-src to 'self'.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the single server-generated page contains no user-derived markup, enforced by nonce-based CSP and exclusive use of textContent.

10.why: Server error responses are generic with no stack traces or private data, but the reset token and MFA code are written to the on-page "Logs" panel and console.log within the owning browser session.

11.why: Passwords (Argon2id) and reset tokens (SHA-256 hashes) are stored securely, but the secret MFA code "482913" is hardcoded in the source and returned in API responses.

12.why: No default credentials can exist since there is no login at all and a strong password policy is enforced, though the universal fixed MFA code effectively acts as a shared code.

13.why: Every sensitive step enforces attempt counters with a 15-minute lockout (3 for recovery requests, 5 for token, password, and MFA verification) and returns 429 when locked.

14.why: The recovery-request endpoint returns the same generic message and issues a token regardless of whether the contact is valid or known, preventing account enumeration.

15.why: The reset code is a 256-bit CSPRNG-generated hex value, unique per recovery, bound to the owning session, single-use, and expiring after 10 minutes.
